name: Bahamas

facts.religion: Christian, mostly Baptist, Anglican and Catholic

snapshot: A tourism and offshore finance archipelago where Philip Davis won a rare second consecutive term for his party in a May 2026 snap election.
culture: Junkanoo, a street parade of costumed dancers, cowbells and goatskin drums held on Boxing Day and New Year's Day, is the heart of Bahamian culture and has roots in the festivities of enslaved Africans. Conch, eaten raw in salads or fried, is the national dish. Rake-and-scrape music uses a saw scraped with a knife.
society: The 700 islands live mainly from tourism, including mega-resorts and cruise ships, and from offshore banking. Hurricane Dorian in 2019 devastated Abaco and Grand Bahama. Many Haitian migrants live in informal settlements, a sensitive political issue. Most Bahamians live on New Providence, around Nassau.
situation: Philip "Brave" Davis of the Progressive Liberal Party became prime minister in 2021. He called an early election for May 2026 and won a second term, the first time in three decades that a Bahamian government had been re-elected.
power: A parliamentary democracy and Commonwealth realm. The prime minister leads the majority in the 41-seat House of Assembly, elected by first past the post.

leaders.state: King Charles III, represented by a governor-general

sources.label: CBC Barbados: Davis guides his party to victory
